written.text: Prove that the bisectors of the angles of a triangle are concurrent. OR Prove that triangles on equal bases and of equal altitudes are equal in area.
modelAnswer: To prove that the bisectors of the angles of a triangle are concurrent:
Let the bisectors of ∠A and ∠B intersect at I.
Since I lies on the bisector of ∠A, d(I,AB)=d(I,AC).
Since I lies on the bisector of ∠B, d(I,AB)=d(I,BC).
Therefore, d(I,AC)=d(I,BC), so I lies on bisector ∠C.
Hence all three angle bisectors are concurrent.
To prove that triangles on equal bases and of equal altitudes are equal in area:
Let b1 and b2 be the base lengths, and h1 and h2 the corresponding altitudes.
Area of the first triangle, A1=1/2 b1h1.
Area of the second triangle, A2=1/2 b2h2.
Therefore, A1=A2, so the triangles are equal in area.
written.followUp: Prove that the medians of a triangle are concurrent. OR Prove that triangles on equal bases and between the same parallels are equal in area.

written.text: Prove that any point equidistant from the end points of a line segment is on the right bisector of it. OR Prove that triangles on equal bases and of equal altitudes are equal in areas.
modelAnswer: Option 1: Let AB be the segment, M its midpoint, and P a point such that PA = PB.
Since AM = BM, PA = PB, and PM = PM (common), △PAM ≅ △PBM by SSS.
Therefore ∠PMA = ∠PMB; as A, M and B are collinear, these equal adjacent angles are each 90°.
Thus PM ⟂ AB and M is the midpoint of AB, so P lies on the perpendicular bisector (right bisector) of AB.
Option 2: Let the equal bases of the two triangles each have length b and their equal altitudes each have length h.
Area of each triangle = 1/2 × b × h.
Therefore, the two triangles have equal areas.

written.text: Prove that the right bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent. OR Prove that triangles on equal bases and of equal altitudes are equal in area.
modelAnswer: Let the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC meet at O.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, OA = OB.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AC, OA = OC.
Therefore, OB = OC, so O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC.
Hence the perpendicular bisectors of the three sides are concurrent at O.
Let the equal bases of the two triangles be b1 and b2, and their equal altitudes be h1 and h2.
Thus b1 = b2 and h1 = h2.
Area of the first triangle, A1 = 1/2 × b1 × h1.
Area of the second triangle, A2 = 1/2 × b2 × h2.
Since b1 = b2 and h1 = h2, A1 = A2.
Hence the triangles are equal in area.

Since I lies on the bisector of ∠B, its perpendicular distances from AB and BC are equal.

Area of the first triangle = 1/2 bh.
Area of the second triangle = 1/2 bh.

written.text: Prove that the right bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent. OR Prove that parallelograms on equal bases and having the same (or equal) altitude are equal in area.
modelAnswer: Option 1: Perpendicular bisectors of the sides are concurrent.
Let the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC meet at O.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, OA = OB.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC, OB = OC.
Hence O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AC as well.
Thus, the three perpendicular bisectors pass through O and are concurrent.
Option 2: Parallelograms on equal bases and with equal altitudes have equal areas.
Let the two parallelograms have equal bases b and equal altitudes h.
Area of the first parallelogram = b × h.
Area of the second parallelogram = b × h.
Therefore, the two parallelograms have equal areas.
written.followUp: Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent, OR prove that parallelograms on equal bases and between the same parallels have equal areas.

written.text: Prove that the right bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent. OR Prove that parallelograms on equal bases and having the same (or equal) altitudes are equal in area.
modelAnswer: Option 1: Concurrency of the perpendicular bisectors
Let the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC meet at O.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, OA = OB.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC, OB = OC.
Therefore OA = OC, so O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AC.
Hence the three perpendicular bisectors pass through O and are concurrent.
Area of a parallelogram = base × altitude.
Let the equal bases of the two parallelograms be b and their equal altitudes be h.
Their areas are b × h and b × h.
Therefore, the parallelograms are equal in area.

written.text: The bisector of the angles of a triangle are concurrent OR Parallelogram on equal bases and having the same ...
modelAnswer: Angle-bisector theorem: Let the bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at I.
Since I lies on the bisector of ∠B, it is equidistant from BA and BC.
Since I lies on the bisector of ∠C, it is equidistant from CB and CA.
Therefore, I is equidistant from BA and CA, so it lies on the bisector of ∠A.
Hence the three angle bisectors are concurrent.
Parallelogram theorem: Let two parallelograms have equal bases and the same altitude.
Area of a parallelogram = base × altitude.
Therefore, the parallelograms have equal areas.

written.text: Prove that the right bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent. OR Prove that triangles on the same base and of the same (i.e. equal) altitudes are equal in area.
modelAnswer: Proof 1: Right bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent.
Let the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC meet at O.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, OA = OB.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC, OB = OC.
Hence, O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AC.
Thus, the perpendicular bisectors of all three sides pass through O and are concurrent.
Proof 2: Triangles on the same base and with equal altitudes have equal areas.
Let the two triangles have the same base b and equal altitudes h.
Area of the first triangle = 1/2 bh.
Area of the second triangle = 1/2 bh.
Therefore, the areas of the two triangles are equal.

written.text: Prove that “The right bisectors of the sides of a triangle are concurrent.” OR Prove that “triangles on the same base and of same (i.e. equal) altitudes are equal in area.”

Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, OA = OB.
Since O lies on the perpendicular bisector of AC, OA = OC.
Therefore OB = OC, so O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC.
Hence the right bisectors of the three sides are concurrent.
Option 2: Let the triangles have common base b and equal altitudes h.
Area of the first triangle = 1/2 bh.
Area of the second triangle = 1/2 bh.
Therefore, the two triangles are equal in area.
